# Rank from largest to smallest
sorted_values = sorted(data.values(), reverse=True)
print(f"\nTop 10 states by UI tax receipts:")
for i, v in enumerate(sorted_values[:10]):
    for state, val in data.items():
        if val == v:
            print(f"  {i+1}. {state}: {v}")
            break

# The Zipf exponent s is estimated by OLS regression:
# log(rank) = A - s * log(size)
# slope = -s, so s = -slope

# Alternatively: log(size) = B - (1/s) * log(rank)
# slope of log(size) vs log(rank) = -1/s, so s = -1/slope

# Standard approach: regress log(rank) on log(size)
n = len(sorted_values)
ranks = list(range(1, n+1))
log_ranks = [math.log(r) for r in ranks]

# OLS slope: sum((x-xbar)*(y-ybar)) / sum((x-xbar)^2)

print(f"\nOLS: log(rank) = A + ({slope_log_rank_vs_log_size:.6f}) * log(size)")
zipf_exponent = -slope_log_rank_vs_log_size
print(f"Zipf exponent s = {zipf_exponent:.6f}")

# Also compute using the alternative method
slope_log_size_vs_log_rank = sum((log_ranks[i] - ybar) * (log_sizes[i] - xbar) for i in range(n)) / sum((log_ranks[i] - ybar)**2 for i in range(n))
zipf_alt = -1 / slope_log_size_vs_log_rank
print(f"Alternative method: s = {zipf_alt:.6f}")

# The standard Zipf's Law: size ~ rank^(-s), so log(size) = const - s*log(rank)
# Regress log(size) on log(rank) to get slope = -s
slope2 = sum((log_ranks[i] - ybar) * (log_sizes[i] - xbar) for i in range(n)) / sum((log_ranks[i] - ybar)**2 for i in range(n))
zipf_direct = -slope2
print(f"Direct method: s = {zipf_direct:.6f}")

# Final answer: round to nearest thousandth
answer = round(zipf_direct, 3)
print(f"\nFinal answer (rounded to nearest thousandth): {answer}")
